summary: WP-006: The substitution of $this->helper->createTranslator() for AppFactory::createDeeplHelper()->createTranslator() is architecturally correct and reduces redundant factory calls. Reading the class shows that _handleActions() (line 76) always assigns $this->helper before calling handleTest() (line 84), making the property reliably populated at point of use. The $helper property is typed as DeeplHelper (not nullable), which is the correct declaration for a property that is always assigned before use. The AppFactory import is not stale — it is still legitimately used on lines 76, 174, and 183. The change is consistent with the general principle of preferring instance properties over repeated static factory calls within the same request lifecycle. Only DeepLTestScreen.php was modified.

comments.note: The $helper property is declared as DeeplHelper (non-nullable, line 27) but is only assigned in _handleActions(). PHP does not enforce initialization of typed non-nullable properties until they are first read, so this is safe at runtime given the call order. However, a strict static analysis tool may flag this as a potentially uninitialized property read. The existing PHPStan baseline absorbs this; if the baseline is regenerated after a clean-up, this may surface. A constructor assignment or nullable type with a null-guard would be the long-term fix.
